Capability-gap development roadmap (item #9, application A7)

Full production run: 2,004 model cards annotated · 5166 gap entries · grouped into 150 capability groups, ranked by the summed priority score of the models each group blocks. Two views: overall, and restricted to structure-formation observables. Source data: models/capability_gaps_full.jsonl; groups: models/capability_gap_roadmap.jsonl.

Definitions — read this first

The idea. Every model card contains routes: recipes for testing that model against data (theory → equations → predicted observable → comparison with measurements). The gap run asked, for every step of every recipe of every model: does the tool to do this step actually exist? Whatever is missing became a gap entry. This page aggregates those entries into a development roadmap: which missing capabilities block the most high-priority models.

capability theme
The shared missing capability behind many model-specific gap descriptions — e.g. every variant of "no Lyman-α likelihood exists for this model's power-spectrum cutoff" lands in the Lyman-α theme. One theme may appear under several gap types (a missing piece of software vs. a missing statistical comparison for the same probe).
gap type
theory — a framework nobody has worked out; derivation — a doable-but-not-done calculation; tool — missing software; simulation — missing N-body/hydro runs; emulator — a fast surrogate for such runs; likelihood — the statistical machinery to compare a prediction with a specific dataset; data — a needed measurement; calibration — an existing method with unmeasured inputs.
priority weight
The sum of the observational-priority scores (adjusted_priority_score from the ranking pass) of the distinct models blocked by the group. A high weight means: closing this one gap unblocks many high-priority models.
severity
blocks_all_observables — the model cannot be confronted with data at all; blocks_key_observables — its most constraining observables are out of reach; degrades_precision — testable, with avoidable error; minor — convenience gap.
effort
small — days-to-weeks for one person; medium — a focused project, months; large — a substantial collaboration effort; major_program — a multi-year program.
structure-formation view
Same groups, but counting only gap entries that block an observable in a structure-formation channel (clusters, dwarf_galaxies, large_scale_structure, lyman_alpha, milky_way_satellites, small_scale_structure, strong_lensing), a route leading to one, or everything for a model that has such observables.

1. Relic-abundance solver extension (micrOMEGAs/MadDM/DarkSUSY)

Cosmic-ray boosted sub-GeV gravitationally interacting dark matter with a spin-2 mediator (arXiv:1912.09904 · priority score 48 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: medium)
The momentum-dependent spin-2 (KK graviton) CR-DM scattering cross section and boosted-flux calculation exist only as a private modification of DarkSUSY; no public code computes dPhi_chi/dT_chi and its Earth attenuation for the G^{mu nu}T_{mu nu} coupling with its strong q^2 dependence.
proposed resolution: Extend the public DarkSUSY CRDM module with the spin-2 mediator differential cross section d(sigma)/dT for CR protons/helium on chi (parameterized by m_chi, m_G, c_SM/Lambda, c_DM/Lambda) and thread the same momentum dependence through the layered-Earth attenuation solver, validating against the paper's O(1e-35) cm^2 benchmark reach.
Inelastic dark matter with a dark photon mediator (arXiv:1911.03176 · priority score 46 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: small)
The FeynRules/CalcHEP model file for the two-state Majorana inelastic dark matter with kinetically mixed dark photon is not confirmed public, blocking off-the-shelf reproduction of the micrOMEGAs coannihilation thermal targets over (m_chi1, Delta, m_A', epsilon, alpha_D).
proposed resolution: Release or re-derive the FeynRules v2.3.32 iDM implementation, export CalcHEP files for micrOMEGAs v5.0.6, and validate against the paper's benchmark thermal targets at m_A'/m_chi1 = 2.5 and 3 with Delta = 0.1 m_chi1.
PQ Dirac-neutrino model with scalar WIMP and axion dark matter (arXiv:2001.01846 · priority score 42 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: small)
No public micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP (or equivalent) implementation of the mixed singlet-doublet scalar sector of this one-loop PQ Dirac-neutrino model exists, so the scalar WIMP freeze-out and sigma_SI cannot be computed beyond the paper's limiting-case benchmarks.
proposed resolution: Implement the eta_u-singlet scalar sector (mass eigenstates, quartic couplings, Higgs and gauge interactions) in FeynRules, export to CalcHEP, and run micrOMEGAs for Omega_S h^2 and sigma_SI across the singlet-doublet mixing plane.
Singlet-doublet freeze-in dark matter in fast-expansion cosmology (arXiv:2301.02514 · priority score 41 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: medium)
No freeze-in relic-abundance solver implements this model's non-standard fast-expansion pre-BBN cosmology; the required Boltzmann integration with a modified H(T) (parameters n, T_r) and decays of thermalized doublet-like states is not available in any public code identified by the card.
proposed resolution: Extend the micrOMEGAs freeze-in module (or a standalone Boltzmann script) to accept a user-defined H(T) = H_std (T/T_r)^(n/2) fast-expansion history, and validate against the relic-density contours in the primary paper benchmarks.
Conformal freeze-in quark-portal dark matter (arXiv:1910.10160 · priority score 40 · severity: minor · effort: medium)
No recast pipeline maps the quark-portal CFT operator (lambda_CFT, Lambda_CFT, d) onto the listed null channels — CMB energy injection, stellar cooling, meson decays, and collider unparticle searches — for couplings above the freeze-in benchmark.
proposed resolution: Assemble a screening recast combining existing unparticle collider limits, stellar-cooling rate formulas, and ExoCLASS-style CMB energy-injection constraints, parameterized by (lambda_CFT, Lambda_CFT, d), validated against the paper's benchmark consistency statement.
Two-Higgs-doublet plus pseudoscalar mediator Majorana dark matter (arXiv:1910.09771 · priority score 40 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: small)
No public code implements the one- and two-loop matching of the 2HDM+a pseudoscalar interactions onto nucleon scalar and gluon operators, which produces the leading (loop-induced) spin-independent signal since the tree-level rate is momentum suppressed; the model's critical direct-detection observable therefore cannot be computed with existing packages like micrOMEGAs, which stop at tree level for this structure.
proposed resolution: Implement the published one- and two-loop Wilson-coefficient formulas (from the primary paper and the pseudoscalar-mediator matching literature, e.g. 1810.01039) as a module feeding DirectDM/DDCalc, validated against the paper's maximum sigma_SI near 5e-47 cm^2 at m_A = 600 GeV.
Supersymmetric B-L neutralino LSP dark matter with metastable cosmic strings (arXiv:1912.03695 · priority score 39 · severity: blocks_key_observables · effort: large)
No public code couples the B-L hybrid-inflation dynamics, tachyonic preheating, heavy-neutrino leptogenesis, B-L-Higgs-to-gravitino decays, and thermal plus nonthermal neutralino production into one scan, so the viable window (v_B-L = 3.0-5.8e15 GeV, m_3/2 = 10 TeV-10 PeV, x about 0.4) cannot be reproduced or extended.
proposed resolution: Build a scan pipeline that combines micrOMEGAs or DarkSUSY for the thermal higgsino/wino relic component with a set of coupled Boltzmann equations for reheating, gravitino production, and B-L Higgs decays (following the paper's equations), validated by recovering the quoted viable window.
Inelastic freeze-in pseudo-Dirac dark matter (arXiv:2304.06072 · priority score 39 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: small)
No public model implementation of the pseudo-Dirac dark-photon freeze-in setup exists; the paper's micrOMEGAs/CalcHEP model files for computing the chi1/chi2 freeze-in yields (including Z-decay contributions) are not released.
proposed resolution: Reimplement the pseudo-Dirac model (chi1, chi2, kinetically mixed A' with off-diagonal current) in CalcHEP/FeynRules and run micrOMEGAs freeze-in routines, validating against the paper's relic-density contours.

proposed resolution: Solve the coupled Boltzmann equations for the phi_1/phi_2/J sector thermalizing through the Higgs portal to obtain Delta N_eff(lambda_1H, v1, v2), then evaluate it against Planck N_eff posteriors with a CLASS-based Majoron cosmology run including late J -> nu nu decays.
7.1 keV sterile-neutrino dark matter with low-scale leptogenesis (arXiv:1412.4899 · score 27)
The full momentum distribution f(p) of sterile neutrinos produced by out-of-equilibrium singlet-scalar decay at T ~ 100 GeV is only approximately known for this model; the primary paper explicitly leaves the detailed free-streaming/velocity analysis beyond scope, blocking any quantitative small-scale-structure statement.
proposed resolution: Derive f(p,T) by solving the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for freeze-in from decays of an initially thermal scalar (standard decay-produced freeze-in formalism), including entropy dilution from T_prod ~ 100 GeV to today, and tabulate it as a psd file for the CLASS ncdm module.
Dark-photon freeze-in Dirac fermion dark matter during early matter domination (arXiv:2204.03670 · score 26)
The card provides only the number-density yield, not the full nonthermal momentum distribution f(p) of chi produced during the EMD era, so the free-streaming length, linear transfer function, and any EMDE-enhanced microhalo prediction cannot be computed.
proposed resolution: Derive f(p) by solving the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for freeze-in during the parameterized EMD (including entropy injection redshifting), then feed it to a Boltzmann code (CLASS with a non-cold relic distribution) to obtain the transfer function and small-scale cutoff/enhancement.
S3 x Z2 sterile-neutrino dark matter model (arXiv:1912.02294 · score 25)
No calculation exists of the S3 x Z2 sterile-neutrino relic abundance and momentum distribution from its actual production channels (feeble scalar-sector Yukawas and the dimension-5 L N_s D phi operator); public sterile-neutrino codes implement only mixing-driven thermal production, so the model's warm/cold classification and DM fraction are undetermined.
proposed resolution: Derive and solve the freeze-in Boltzmann equation at the distribution-function level for N_s production via the S3 x Z2 scalar and Yukawa couplings (e.g. extend a freeze-in phase-space code or write a dedicated momentum-dependent solver as done for scotogenic FIMPs), outputting f(p) and Omega h^2 over the keV-MeV mass range; feed f(p) into CLASS to obtain the transfer function.
MiTeVeS Noether-current mimetic dark matter cosmology (arXiv:2107.12161 · score 25)
Linear cosmological perturbation theory for MiTeVeS (scalar/vector/mimetic sector sound speed, closure relations, and growth equations) has not been derived, and consequently no Boltzmann-solver implementation exists, so no large-scale-structure or growth prediction can be made; the paper explicitly defers perturbations to future work.
proposed resolution: Derive the linearized field equations for the mimetic scalar-vector sector around FLRW (including the effective sound speed c_s and any anisotropic stress), then implement them in a modified Einstein-Boltzmann code such as a CLASS or hi_class extension to output the matter power spectrum and growth rate for comparison with clustering data.
SU(3) x U(1) ten-plet accident dark matter (arXiv:2307.10092 · score 25)
The spin-independent scalar-nucleon cross section for the six-state ten-plet multiplet through the Higgs portal has not been computed, so LZ/XENON-class direct-detection limits cannot be applied to this model.
proposed resolution: Derive the per-component Higgs-portal scalar-nucleon cross section (standard scalar-portal formula weighted by the multiplet composition and local abundance fractions from the multi-component relic calculation) and recast published xenon-experiment limits onto the (m_DM, lambda_H) plane.
BSTV scalar-field oscillation cold dark matter (arXiv:astro-ph/0502222 · score 25)
The soft-boson non-accumulation condition is stated only qualitatively via a de Broglie-wavelength argument; no linear transfer function or clustering calculation for the oscillating q quanta exists to quantify where the scalar CDM does or does not cluster on galaxy scales.
proposed resolution: Derive the perturbation equations for the oscillating scalar amplitude in the evolving quadratic effective potential and compute its Jeans/de Broglie suppression scale as a function of boson mass, giving a quantitative galactic-accumulation criterion.
MSM sterile-neutrino WDM from heavier-field decay (arXiv:1308.1109 · score 24)
The decay-produced sterile-neutrino momentum distribution from the heavier MSM field is only available as an approximate analytic form; a Boltzmann-level computation of f(q) for the specific parent decay history (parent abundance, decay rate, entropy evolution) is missing.
proposed resolution: Implement the decay-production Boltzmann equation for the parent field (following existing public FIMP/decay-spectrum solvers such as the Merle-Totzauer approach) and tabulate f(q) for direct input into the CLASS/CAMB ncdm module.
Kination non-equilibrium Majorana dark matter production (arXiv:1704.01056 · score 24)
The nonthermal dark-matter momentum distribution f(p) from out-of-equilibrium production during kination has not been derived (the card tracks number density only and marks distribution_function_available no), so the free-streaming scale and small-scale cutoff k_cut for this branch cannot be computed.
proposed resolution: Derive f(p) by solving the unintegrated production Boltzmann equation over the kination era (production kinematics from the radiation bath, then redshifting through reheating), and implement the result as a non-cold ncdm species in CLASS to obtain the transfer-function cutoff.
Cosmic-selection-rule SU(N)d glueball dark matter (arXiv:1704.02347 · score 24)
The model's linear structure-formation behavior is entirely uncomputed (transfer function and CDM-likeness unknown, no glueball f(p)); evaluating the dark-radiation/structure observable requires mapping the pre-confinement relativistic dark-gluon epoch and the post-confinement glueball fluid onto CMB and LSS perturbation variables, which no existing interacting-dark-radiation implementation covers with a confinement transition.
proposed resolution: Extend a CLASS-based interacting-dark-radiation (ETHOS-like) implementation with a time-dependent transition at the dark confinement temperature, converting self-coupled dark-gluon radiation with temperature ratio T_dark/T_SM into a cold or warm glueball fluid, then compare against Planck and LSS data.
Colored t-channel mediator freeze-in plus superWIMP dark matter (arXiv:1809.10135 · score 24)
No implementation of the exact nonthermal dark matter momentum distribution combining the freeze-in component (from mediator decays and scatterings) and the late superWIMP decay component; the card records only an approximate phase-space treatment, and the Ly-alpha constraint currently relies on a thermal-WDM proxy.
proposed resolution: Derive the full phase-space distribution f(q) by integrating the unintegrated freeze-in and superWIMP decay Boltzmann equations (as done in tools like the FIMP module of micrOMEGAs or a dedicated code in the style of Ballesteros et al. freeze-in distribution calculations), then feed it to CLASS as a non-cold dark matter species to obtain the model-specific transfer function.
Scalar dark matter from Q-ball decay (arXiv:2304.07462 · score 24)
No linear transfer function exists for the nonthermal scalar spectrum produced by Q-ball decay, whose injection momentum is set by the Q-ball angular frequency rather than a thermal bath, so the thermal-WDM 5.3 keV bound cannot be applied without recasting.
proposed resolution: Derive the decay-produced phase-space distribution f(q) for scalars emitted from Q-ball decay at the decay temperature and pass it to the CLASS/CAMB non-cold-relic (ncdm) module as a tabulated distribution to obtain model-specific transfer functions across the (m_chi, K, Q) parameter space.
Interacting scalar-field dark matter and early dark energy (arXiv:2402.08815 · score 24)
The coupling Q = beta phidot^2 psidot^2 is imposed at the conservation-equation level without a microscopic action, and the card flags possible stability and prior pathologies of the perturbed energy-transfer terms outside the worked examples; no derived stability/viability conditions delimit the (m_phi, lambda_phi, beta) space over which the Boltzmann solution is trustworthy.
proposed resolution: Derive the gauge-consistent perturbed energy-momentum transfer and its no-ghost/gradient-stability conditions for this coupling (following the interacting-dark-energy instability literature), encode the resulting viability bounds as hard priors in the MCMC, and add runtime stability checks to the public modified CLASS.
Low-reheating warm neutralino dark matter (arXiv:hep-ph/0607012 · score 24)
The full nonthermal neutralino phase-space distribution f(p) from scalar-decay cascades is not derived; the card only gives the single warmness parameter r_chi, which is insufficient input for a Boltzmann transfer-function calculation or a defensible mapping to thermal-WDM limits.
proposed resolution: Derive f(p) by integrating the decay-injection spectrum (scalar decay to SUSY cascades to neutralinos) over the scalar decay history without the instantaneous-decay approximation, and tabulate it as a psd file for CLASS/CAMB non-cold-relic (ncdm) input.
Two-24 type III GMSB gravitino warm dark matter variant (arXiv:0807.4524 · score 24)

proposed resolution: Derive the gravitino momentum distribution by integrating the thermal scattering production rate over the reheating history and adding the NLSP-decay component, following standard nonthermal-relic phase-space calculations, and tabulate f(q) as an ncdm input for CLASS.
Nearly supersymmetric atomic dark matter (arXiv:1009.3523 · score 23)
No linear transfer function exists for this model: the dark plasma undergoes dark acoustic oscillations and Coulomb-coupled damping before dark recombination, but the card records transfer_function_shape and all structure-formation entries as unknown, with no phase-space distribution or Boltzmann-hierarchy implementation.
proposed resolution: Derive the tight-coupling dark-photon/dark-baryon perturbation equations for this sector and implement them in CLASS via an ETHOS-like parameterization (dark-radiation interaction rates from alpha_D and constituent masses), producing P(k) with the dark-acoustic-oscillation scale and Silk-like damping.
U(1)_B-L right-handed-neutrino dark matter (arXiv:1104.2384 · score 23)
No momentum distribution f_N(p) has been derived for N_1 produced by thermal freeze-out followed by entropy dilution from heavy RHN decay (with possible Z_B-L-mediated interactions), so the free-streaming input to structure-formation constraints is undefined for this model.
proposed resolution: Derive the redshifted post-dilution N_1 spectrum semi-analytically (thermal spectrum at freeze-out diluted by the computed S ~ 160 entropy factor), tabulate it, and feed it to CLASS/CAMB as a non-cold-dark-matter psd file to obtain the linear transfer function.
FIMP dark matter from flavon portals (arXiv:2305.03167 · score 23)
No full non-thermal momentum distribution f(q) for the FIMP including both flavon-decay and scattering production channels; the paper's free-streaming length is a decay-only indicative estimate, so linear-power suppression predictions are unreliable.
proposed resolution: Derive f(q) by integrating the unintegrated freeze-in Boltzmann equation with both S/h_S/A_S decay and 2->2 scattering source terms (standard freeze-in distribution formalism), then feed the tabulated distribution into CLASS as a non-cold ncdm species to get the exact transfer function instead of a free-streaming-length proxy.
Leptophilic light flavon hot-relic model (arXiv:1812.10963 · score 22)
The non-thermal momentum distribution of the freeze-in-produced eta is not derived (distribution_function_available: no), so the mixed hot+cold transfer function cannot be computed accurately for the freeze-in regime at large v_phi.
proposed resolution: Solve the unintegrated Boltzmann equation for freeze-in production through the charged-lepton couplings to obtain f_eta(q), and feed it into a Boltzmann solver's non-cold species (CLASS ncdm with a tabulated distribution) to get the subcomponent transfer function.
R-parity violating axino warm dark matter (arXiv:1403.1782 · score 21)
The axino phase-space distribution f_axino(q) from thermal production after reheating (as a function of T_R, f_a, m_axino) is only approximate and never tabulated, yet it is the required input for the transfer-function step and for any warmness statement beyond a crude thermal-WDM analogy.
proposed resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for axino production from thermal-bath scatterings (freeze-in/thermal-production treatment as in the related 1707.06418-style calculations) over the (T_R, f_a) benchmark region and release tabulated f(q) files consumable by CLASS ncdm.

The full decay-product phase-space distribution f(q) for S from chi -> S S (including the redshifting of the decay-injected momentum for the relevant y and T_dec range) has not been derived, so no linear transfer function or free-streaming suppression scale exists beyond the paper's rough nonrelativistic-by-1-keV criterion.
proposed resolution: Derive f(q) analytically for two-body decays of the nonrelativistic chi population as a function of y, m_S/m_chi, and decay time, tabulate it as a non-cold-dark-matter distribution file, and run CLASS or CAMB in ncdm mode to obtain the model's transfer function and half-mode scale across the parameter space.

Only a representative 0.1c recoil speed exists; the full Hawking-recoil velocity distribution from the final evaporation stage of the regular metric, and the resulting remnant free-streaming length and matter-power suppression, have not been derived, blocking the coldness/structure-formation observable.
proposed resolution: Compute final-stage emission spectra for the regular black-hole family (extend BlackHawk with the regular metric's greybody factors and finite-temperature endpoint), build the recoil velocity distribution over formation times, and feed it as a non-cold-DM momentum distribution into CLASS/CAMB to obtain the transfer function and free-streaming bound.

proposed resolution: Derive f(p) by integrating the scalaron decay rate over the reheating history (standard inflaton-decay distribution techniques give a quasi-analytic result), parameterized by (m_X, xi_X, xi_h), in a form usable as a CLASS/CAMB ncdm input table.

proposed resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation for the phi distribution with lambda phi^4 2-to-2 and 4-to-2 collision terms starting from the gap_1 tachyonic spectrum (extending existing dark-freeze-out/cannibal-sector Boltzmann codes), mapping out in (xi, lambda, m_phi) where instantaneous chemical equilibrium is a valid approximation.

The phase-space distribution f(q) of the scalaron-decay-produced massive vector is not available (distribution_function_available: no), so the free-streaming and transfer-function calculation cannot go beyond the rough L_FS estimate.
proposed resolution: Derive the decay-produced momentum distribution for two-body scalaron decay through the Starobinsky reheating history (standard inflaton-decay f(q) techniques) and supply it as a tabulated non-cold-DM distribution to CLASS/CAMB ncdm modules to compute the model's transfer function.

proposed resolution: Derive the dark-baryon phase-space distribution after confinement of the secluded thermal dark sector (thermal distribution at T_D with mass ~ Lambda_c) and establish the mapping to an equivalent thermal-WDM mass so existing WDM bounds can be reused.

The cosmological evolution of the relativistic screening species, and hence the redshift dependence of the screening length r_s(z) that the simulations need as input, is not derived; the card flags production of the screening population as an unresolved difficulty and no linear-theory (Boltzmann) treatment of the scale-dependent growth is provided.
proposed resolution: Derive the coupled scalar-plus-screening-species background and linear perturbation equations and implement them as a modified CLASS species, yielding r_s(z) and consistent initial conditions/transfer functions for the N-body step.

proposed resolution: Derive the primordial momentum distribution and power spectrum of the longitudinal vector modes produced during inflation (Graham-Mardon-Rajendran-type calculation for m_f ~ 1 MeV, H_inf ~ 1.6e11 GeV), then feed the resulting f(p) or transfer function into a modified CLASS/CAMB run to verify CDM-like behavior and any small-scale isocurvature bump.

The momentum-space phase-space distribution f(q) of freeze-in DFSZ axinos produced through the Kim-Nilles axino-Higgsino-Higgs (mu/f_a) and axino-top-stop (m_t/f_a) channels is not derived; without it neither the warmness of light axinos nor the transfer-function suppression can be computed for this specific channel mix.
proposed resolution: Solve the momentum-dependent freeze-in Boltzmann equation for the two-body Higgs/Higgsino decay and stop-scattering collision terms (following the treatment used for freeze-in axino distributions in the related 1707.06418-style analyses), tabulate f(q) versus m_axino, f_a, mu, and the Higgs/Higgsino/stop spectrum, and feed it to the CLASS ncdm module to obtain the model-specific transfer function.

Heavy-scalar-decay non-thermal warm dark matter (arXiv:2305.15736 · priority score 50 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: large)
Nonlinear predictions (subhalo mass function, satellite counts) rely on thermal-WDM-calibrated simulations through an approximate half-mode-scale matching; no N-body simulations exist for the broader, higher-momentum-peaked decay-produced spectra, so the mapping's validity outside the studied f(q) grid is uncontrolled.
proposed resolution: Run a small suite of cosmological N-body simulations initialized with the modified-CLASS nonthermal transfer functions (and thermal velocities drawn from f(q)) for a few benchmark m_nonthermal values, and calibrate the subhalo mass function against the thermal-WDM equivalents to validate or correct the half-mode mapping.
Two-state inelastic self-interacting dark matter (arXiv:1805.03203 · priority score 46 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: large)
All existing simulations for this benchmark are dark-matter-only; the card notes baryonic feedback is a major missing ingredient for mapping the predicted cores and satellite depletion onto observed Milky Way dwarfs.
proposed resolution: Run zoom-in hydrodynamical simulations of Milky Way-like halos with the inelastic two-state scattering module coupled to an established galaxy-formation model (e.g. Auriga/IllustrisTNG physics in Arepo), spanning the benchmark (sigma/m, Delta/m_chi) grid.

proposed resolution: Run dedicated simulations of the scalar-mediated instability (coupled fermion-fluid plus scalar-field dynamics, e.g. an adapted cosmological hydrodynamics or N-body plus scalar solver) to obtain the post-formation nugget mass spectrum and the calibrated cutoff transfer function as a function of m_phi and z_F.

No cosmological hydrodynamic simulations exist for the N_sec-copy dissipative dark sector, so satellite abundance/planarity, the field-galaxy velocity function, and baryon-correlated halo structure predictions rest on idealized steady-state arguments (the card marks simulation_calibrated partial).
proposed resolution: Extend a galaxy-formation hydrodynamics code (e.g. GIZMO or AREPO) with a second dissipative fluid carrying dark-electromagnetic cooling and kinetic-mixing supernova heating, and run zoom-in simulations of Milky-Way-like and dwarf halos across the N_sec, epsilon parameter plane.
Dark Dimension KK-graviton dark matter (arXiv:2311.05318 · priority score 37 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: large)
No N-body simulations or calibrated nonlinear prescription exist for kick-velocity dark gravitons, which the paper states is beyond its scope; this forces the conservative linear-scale cut (k_NL,0 ~ 0.09 Mpc^-1) in the KiDS analysis and blocks any subhalo or Milky-Way satellite predictions.
proposed resolution: Run N-body simulations with initial conditions and late-time velocity kicks matching the tower decay history (in the style of existing decaying-DM recoil simulations), calibrate a halofit-like nonlinear correction and subhalo mass-function suppression versus v0, enabling full-scale weak-lensing and satellite-count likelihoods.

The combined effect of a damped initial power spectrum plus velocity-dependent self-interactions (1-10 cm^2/g at dwarf velocities) on satellite counts, subhalo mass functions, and dwarf central densities is uncalibrated by simulations for this model class.
proposed resolution: Run ETHOS-style N-body simulations with the model's truncated transfer function and a velocity-dependent SIDM cross section to calibrate the subhalo mass function and core-size relations, then fit a semi-analytic halo-response model for parameter scans.
Hidden dark matter cosmology (HiDM) (arXiv:2305.08943 · priority score 35 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: large)
No N-body simulations calibrate the nonlinear (sub)halo mass function for HiDM initial conditions (the card states simulation_calibrated: no), so the transition-dependent suppression mass scale M_sup and satellite/lensing predictions rest on linear-theory extrapolation.
proposed resolution: Run a small suite of cosmological N-body simulations (with thermal-velocity or suppressed-power initial conditions drawn from the HiDM transfer functions) spanning R_eq^T, and fit a halo/subhalo mass-function suppression formula analogous to existing WDM calibrations.
Pseudoscalar-mediated neutrino-interacting Dirac dark matter (arXiv:1602.07624 · priority score 34 · severity: degrades_precision · effort: large)
The mapping from the linear DAO cutoff to nonlinear halo and subhalo mass functions is not simulation-calibrated for this model (card: simulation_calibrated no); existing ETHOS N-body calibrations cover only a few benchmark parameter points, not this pseudoscalar-mediator parameter region.
proposed resolution: Run a small suite of ETHOS-style cosmological zoom simulations spanning the model's T_kd/M_cut range and fit a (sub)halo mass-function suppression formula in terms of the DAO scale and damping envelope, enabling satellite-count predictions without per-point simulations.
